brief: Franco-German 10yr spreads widened +32bps to 141bps last week, the biggest widening since 1990, as forced OAT deleveraging after large VAR swings turned a real but already-known French fiscal problem into disorderly price action, briefly hitting +160bps intraday Friday before a soft US payrolls print defused the panic. DB sees OATs 40-50bps cheap but is not yet buying them outright, and reads the sell-off's political pressure as more likely to force credible French reform than to start a fresh euro crisis; the ECB terminal rate has already slumped toward 2.75-3% from 3.5% priced eight days ago as a result. Friday's September payrolls miss (+29k vs +133k expected, soft wages) cut Fed October hike odds from 64% to 23% and ECB odds from 42% to 14%, even though DB still expects two more 25bp Fed hikes given resilient participation and unemployment data. Brazil's Bolsonaro led Lula in the first round, pointing to an October 25 runoff and an expected DI-rates rally as election premium unwinds. Brent rose +4.94% on the contract roll while European diesel fell -7.31% last week on a G7 plan to release oil and diesel reserves.
